DESIGN.outcomes: UNLINKED_SUPPORT (repair) · CITED_AS_CONTRAST (do not repair; INFO; says why and prints the sentence) · UNCLASSIFIED (WARN; a human reads the sentence) · UNCHECKED (unchanged)
DESIGN.two_sign_rule: CITED_AS_CONTRAST requires BOTH, in the same sentence: (1) ATTRIBUTION, structural and language-free — the sentence names another claim AND the owning record's own Claim links declares that other claim; (2) OPPOSITION — a difference/opposition stem (Italian and English). Exactly one sign -> UNCLASSIFIED. Neither -> UNLINKED_SUPPORT, as before.
DESIGN.why_the_lexicon_cannot_shrink_the_check_: The lexicon can only PROMOTE a pair that already has structural attribution. A missed phrasing leaves the pair UNCLASSIFIED, which is a WARN — louder than CITED_AS_CONTRAST (INFO), never quieter. A stray marker word in a supporting sentence without attribution yields UNCLASSIFIED, never contrast, so it cannot suppress a real unlinked-support finding. A CORPUS-STUB declares no links, so a stub-owned pair can never be classified as contrast.
DESIGN.multi_sentence: A PMID cited in several sentences takes the most demanding verdict: any sentence with no sign -> UNLINKED_SUPPORT; contrast only when every citing sentence is a contrast.
DESIGN.scope: Sentence, split on .;!? before a non-lowercase non-digit character, and on the registry's 🔴 statement marker. Over-splitting can only lose the attribution sign (-> toward UNCLASSIFIED), never manufacture contrast.
DESIGN.residual_limit_stated: The opposition sign is still a lexicon. It is stems, not phrases, and bilingual, but it is not semantics. Its failure is bounded, not eliminated: a contrast phrased with no marker AND no attribution to a linked claim still reports UNLINKED_SUPPORT (the pre-change behaviour), which is why every CONTRAST/UNCLASSIFIED line carries the sentence.
